source_refs.note: 2- Peritoneal Dialysis: a main subheading of 14.3.3 Kidney Failure, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 21-21.

blocks.text: Peritoneal dialysis involves the use of peritoneal membrane that lines the abdominal cavity. In this process, 1.5 to 2 litre of dialysate is infused into the patient's abdomen through a catheter. The dialysate is left in abdomen for 4 to 6 hours. Waste products and excess fluid from the blood capillaries of peritoneum pass into the dialysate. Then, the dialysate is drained out of the abdomen and discarded. This process is repeated several times a day, to achieve adequate clearance of waste products and excess fluid.
